title: Measuring What Matters: Synthetic Benchmarks for Concept Bottleneck Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.04326v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Concept bottleneck models predict using high-level concepts detected in inputs. Although these models provide a simple way to reap benefits from interpretability, they are hard to train and evaluate because very few real-world datasets include concept labels. In this paper, we develop synthetic benchmarks for concept bottleneck models. With our benchmarks, researchers can generate labeled datasets and control properties that affect performance, such as data modality, the choice of concepts, or annotation quality. They can thus find problems that suit these models and isolate the factors behind their failures. We demonstrate how our benchmarks can be used to evaluate major use cases for concept bottleneck models: decision support, i.e., helping human experts make better decisions; and automation, i.e., handling routine tasks without supervision. translated_title: 衡量真正重要的东西：概念瓶颈模型的合成基准
translated_abstract: 概念瓶颈模型利用从输入中检测到的高级概念进行预测。尽管这些模型提供了一种从可解释性中获益的简单方式，但由于现实世界中包含概念标签的数据集非常少，它们难以训练和评估。在本文中，我们为概念瓶颈模型开发了合成基准。借助我们的基准，研究人员可以生成带标签的数据集，并控制影响性能的属性，例如数据模态、概念的选择或标注质量。因此，他们可以找到适合这些模型的问题，并分离出导致其失败的因素。我们展示了如何使用我们的基准来评估概念瓶颈模型的主要应用场景：决策支持（即帮助人类专家做出更好的决策）和自动化（即在无监督情况下处理常规任务）。我们的演示展示了这些基准如何识别新的失败模式和归因问题。
tldr: 本文提出了概念瓶颈模型的合成基准，使研究人员能够控制数据模态、概念选择和标注质量等因素，从而系统地评估该类模型在决策支持与自动化场景中的表现，并识别出新的失败模式。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces synthetic benchmarks for concept bottleneck models, enabling researchers to control factors such as data modality, concept choice, and annotation quality to systematically evaluate these models in decision support and automation scenarios and identify new failure modes.
